items.text: The online adventure kits gave our kids something to look forward to when we couldn’t be together in person. It still felt like CYP showed up for us.
Camp helped me grow as a leader and feel connected to other military kids.
items.author: STP youth, 2025

items.text: These events remind us that we’re part of something bigger — a community that understands the Guard life.
During deployment, CYP gave our kids something to smile about — and reminded them they weren’t the only ones missing someone.
This camp put the light back in my daughter’s eyes.
Camp brightened her smile again and gave her friends who understand deployment.
Even online, I felt connected — like other military kids were doing the same thing with me at home.
The adventure kits brought the fun and creativity of CYP right into our living room — a reminder that we’re not alone in this Guard life.
Virtual kits like these keep our Guard families engaged and supported, no matter where duty takes them.
It’s where I meet other Guard kids who get what it’s like when your parent is gone for drill or deployment.
We come for the fun, but we leave feeling connected and seen.
CYP builds community in a way that strengthens readiness — by making sure no Guard family feels isolated.
When Dad was deployed, CYP made me feel proud to be a military kid instead of just missing him.
Having an event during deployment helped break up the long months and gave us a reason to laugh together.
Programs like these don’t just fill the time — they hold families together during the hardest seasons of service.
Even from the command level, I see that CYP keeps readiness high by making sure no family feels left behind.
